title: Issue reverts and escalation are complete

source.note: Runtime facts were not recorded; the turn is assumed to have ended cleanly with nothing in flight.

messages.text: revert c788c91b50 and push pls
I'll look at the commit first, then revert it on master and push.
Working tree is clean on master. The commit is a regular (non-merge) commit, so a plain `git revert` applies.
continue
Continuing: I'll revert the commit, then push to origin/master.
The fetch failed. Let me check the remote configuration.
SSH auth is refused in this environment. I'll do the revert locally first, then try pushing over HTTPS through the `gh` credential helper without changing the remote config.
HTTPS works. Remote master has moved past local. Let me check whether local is simply behind.
Local is only behind, so I'll fast-forward. Two newer commits touch the same files, including one that extends the engine profile, so the revert may conflict.
The revert conflicts because a later commit, #3818, built on the same plan, test file, and `src/lib.rs` code. I need to see what #3818 changed before deciding how to resolve.
You chose to revert both. I'll revert #3818 first, then c788c91b50, so each applies against the code it introduced.
Both reverts applied cleanly. The default revert messages lack the attribution line and a reason, so I'll recreate the two local commits with proper messages before verifying the build.
Now I'll confirm the reverted tree compiles, covering the facade library and the policy test suite that lost a module.
when pushed, close #3817, then reopen the respective tickets from the reverted commits and explain what happened. mark them Escalated as well
The build check passed and nothing else depends on the removed code. Next I'll push, then look up #3817 and the issues tied to the two reverted commits.
Push succeeded. The two commits came from PRs #3805 and #3818. I'll find the issues those PRs closed through the GraphQL API, since this `gh` is too old for that field, and check the Escalated label.
Neither PR formally closed an issue. PR #3805 says it "relates to #3792". I'll check #3818's references and the current state of #3792.
Both PRs reference only #3792, and #3792 was never closed, so there is nothing to reopen. I'll comment on #3792 and label it escalated, then close #3817 with a pointer to the reverts.
The comment and label on #3792 worked. This `gh` version has no `--comment` flag on close, so I'll post the comment and close the issue separately.

The reverts are pushed to master and #3817 is closed. Nothing needed reopening: both reverted commits only referenced #3792, which was still open, so I marked it escalated and explained the reverts there.

**What was pushed:** I reverted two commits, not one, because you chose that when the single revert conflicted. A later commit from PR #3818 had built on c788c91b50 in the same profile function, tests and ExecPlan. Reverting it first let c788c91b50 revert cleanly.

| Revert commit | Reverts | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1969c1f75 | 563e2bd16, which added `normal-and-exceptional-exit` | PR #3818 |
| b1f008583 | c788c91b50, which added `structural-match` and moved the bootstrap | PR #3805 |

The facade library and the policy test suite still type-check. I did not run the tests. SSH push was refused in this environment, so I pushed over HTTPS with the GitHub CLI token and left the remote config unchanged.

**GitHub changes:**
- **#3817** is closed. Its comment names both reverts.
- **#3792** now has the escalated label and a comment. The comment says what was reverted and why, which tests and ExecPlan went with it, and that the cause of the slowdown is still unknown. It also asks for a passing quick performance check before the work lands again.

**Still open:**
- **Unconfirmed fix:** the reverts should end the slowdown, but the next run of the quick performance check on master has not confirmed it yet.
- **#3792 assignment:** it is still assigned to David Baker Effendi and still has the agent-in-progress label. I left both alone because the issue belongs to them.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- When a later commit builds on the one you want to revert, revert them newest first. Each revert then applies to exactly the code that commit introduced, so neither needs hand-editing.
- `gh` on this machine is old. `gh issue close` has no `--comment` flag, and fields such as `closingIssuesReferences` need the GraphQL API.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
